title: Magnetic Phone Chargers for Stiff or Shaky Hands: How They Work and What They Cost
subtitle: A small connector that stays in your phone lets a charging cable snap on by magnet, which may mean less fiddling at the port.
excerpt: If plugging in your phone each night is a fiddly chore, a magnetic charging cable may help. Here's how they work, what the pricing looks like and what they can't do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Charging a phone sounds simple until your hands don't cooperate. The charging port is small, and lining up a plug and pushing it in can take several tries when your fingers are stiff or shaky.

There's a second worry, too. The Active Hands Company, a seller of grip aids, says on its product page that "forcing it at bad angles can lead to damage for your phone and cable." A magnetic charging cable is one way to cut down on the fiddling at the port. If your hands are painful or shaky, it's also worth asking your doctor or an occupational therapist what else might help.
A magnetic setup has two parts. The first is a small connector that goes into your phone's charging port. The second is a cable with a magnetic end that clings to that connector.

The connector is meant to stay put. In The Active Hands Company's words: "Insert the connector into your phone once and leave it there." After that, the maker says the cable snaps on magnetically at any angle. When you're done, you pull the cable away and the connector stays in the phone.

The two products below take different routes. The Active Hands Company sells a magnetic cable and a phone connector, and you buy one of each. VOLTA sells a magnetic USB-C adapter that its page says can turn an existing cable magnetic.

A magnetic cable only helps at the phone end. Plugging a cable into a wall adapter or a power bank still takes a decent grip, so you may want a family member to set that part up. These are cables, not wireless chargers.

There are other trade-offs. The connector sits in your phone's port all the time, which adds one more small part that could wear. The magnetic tips are also a second place where something could fail, and they may need replacing someday. Neither page we're using gives a warranty length.

items: Match the connector to your phone. The Active Hands page lists Lightning for iPhone 5 to iPhone 14 (and some iPads), USB-C for most new phones including iPhone 15 onward, and microUSB for older devices.

Check the full price. Active Hands lists connectors from $4.00 and the cable at $10.95 each, with duties added at checkout for US customers. The page doesn't show a US total, so confirm it at checkout. VOLTA says shipping is calculated at checkout.
Look at cable length and head. The Active Hands cable is 2 meters long, in black, red or purple, and its head rotates 180 degrees so you can hold the phone while it charges.
Check for a USB-C port if you're considering the VOLTA adapter. Its page says a device with a USB-C port becomes a magnetic port, and it doesn't mention Lightning or iPhone-specific compatibility.
Ask about returns and warranty. The product pages don't state a return policy or warranty length, so ask the seller before you order.
Ask your doctor or an occupational therapist if hand pain or tremor makes other parts of daily life hard, too.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well
Setup is a one-time job, and it's a good one to hand to a family member. The connector goes into the phone once and is meant to stay there.

Plug the other end of the cable into a wall adapter in a spot you can reach easily. From then on, bring the magnetic end up to the phone and let it snap on. Make sure the phone starts charging the first time you try it.

Make sure the connector matches your phone before you order. The Active Hands connectors are sold by phone port type, and the VOLTA adapter needs a USB-C port. Confirm the final US total, including duties and shipping, at checkout.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A magnetic cable won't fix every frustration with a phone, but it may make the nightly plug-in easier. If it saves you a few tries each evening, it could be a small purchase worth considering.

products.name: Magnetic Phone Charger (cable plus connector)
products.price: From $4.00 for a connector; magnetic cable $10.95 each (list prices, November 2026). Duties are added at checkout for US customers; the US total isn't shown on the page.
products.blurb: Suits people who want a complete cable-and-connector setup, as long as the connector matches the phone: Lightning (iPhone 5 to 14), USB-C or microUSB. You buy one cable and one connector separately; the cable is 2 meters long and its head rotates 180 degrees. The seller is UK-based.

products.name: Volta Mag Adapter
products.blurb: Suits people with a USB-C phone or tablet who'd rather keep using a cable they already own, since it turns an existing cable magnetic. The page lists MacBook, iPad, Android and Steam Deck and doesn't name iPhones or Lightning. It also mentions two versions without describing them, so check which one you're buying.
